key_insight: This paper argues that evaluating diffusion transformers only on ImageNet class-conditional generation gives an incomplete and potentially misleading picture of progress. It introduces a more holistic benchmark approach, highlighting that text-to-image evaluation is now practical enough to include in standard assessment.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the over-reliance on a single benchmark for diffusion transformer evaluation, which makes it hard to tell whether lower FID scores reflect genuine advances in generative modeling or just optimization for one narrow task.
method: Proposes DiffusionBench as a broader evaluation framework for diffusion transformers.
Introduces NanoGen to make text-to-image training and evaluation more accessible and less costly.
Compares model performance across more realistic and diverse generation settings rather than only ImageNet class-conditional generation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work encourages more reliable model selection by measuring performance on tasks closer to real-world use. It can help shift the field toward evaluations that better capture true generative quality and generalization.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of ImageNet-only evaluation vs. holistic benchmark coverage
Benchmark pipeline diagram showing class-conditional and text-to-image evaluation paths
Metric dashboard with FID and other generation quality indicators
Icon set representing cost, accessibility, diversity, and realism
paper_title: DiffusionBench: On Holistic Evaluation of Diffusion Transformers
paper_authors: Xingjian Leng, Jaskirat Singh, Zhanhao Liang, Ethan Smith, Martin Bell
